A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DS-STAR research, with the original algorithm, benchmark tables, execution trace, and prompts identifiable across versions. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original DS-STAR evaluations on DABStep, KramaBench, and DA-Code, component ablations, refinement sensitivity, and cost measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds report-generation evaluations, verifier sensitivity experiments, additional model evaluations, and spreadsheet and SQL demonstrations.

M1.justification: v4 adds DS-STAR+ (Section 3.2; Algorithm 2), which generates sub-questions, solves them using DS-STAR, writes a report citing the answers, and iteratively generates further questions to expand that report. This substantially changes the supported inference procedure and outputs. The original DS-STAR planning, verification, routing, and debugging pipeline remains intact.

E1.justification: The original three benchmarks remain, while DABStep-Research adds comprehensive report-writing tasks across five categories, including open-ended investigation. v4 also demonstrates a BIRD california_schools SQL task and a manually constructed spreadsheet requiring identification of three separate table regions (Appendices F and H). These extend task and input-condition coverage.

E2.justification: DeepAnalyze-8B is added to the DABStep comparison and serves as the comparator for report generation. The expanded compatibility comparison includes ReAct and Open Data Scientist alongside DS-STAR using DeepSeek-V3 (Table 5). Original benchmark comparator sets otherwise remain largely unchanged; I2I-Agent corresponds to the earlier Mphasis-I2I-Agents entry.

E3.justification: The new report evaluation uses 1–5 content/format scores and pairwise preferences from Gemini-3-Pro and GPT-5, with candidate order reversed between judgments. DS-STAR+ uses Gemini-2.5-Pro for writing, Gemini-2.5-Flash for other modules, and one report-refinement round. Additional experiments vary the verifier model and inputs. These are new protocols; the original Gemini-2.5-Pro, 20-round benchmark setup is retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds a verification-design ablation comparing sequential sufficiency checking against full-plan generation with execution-only feedback, plus verifier-model and input sensitivity tests (Table 4; Appendix A). It also tests report refinement, DeepSeek-V3 compatibility, and complex spreadsheet parsing. The earlier analyzer/router ablations and refinement sensitivity remain; the earlier README-focused Excel example is replaced by broader spreadsheet demonstrations.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly specifies two judgments per report pair with reversed candidate order, adding a limited repeated-evaluation practice for positional-bias control. This does not establish repeated independent report-generation runs. Neither version reports benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests, and the statistical tests and seeds inside retained task examples are unchanged.

E6.justification: Original main scores remain unchanged, including 45.24% DABStep hard accuracy, 44.69% KramaBench accuracy, and 38.5 DA-Code score. New results include 89% and 88% report preference rates under the two judges, 68% preference for refined reports, verifier-ablation results, and latency measurements. Table 9 also introduces a ReAct easy accuracy of 69.33%, inconsistent with 69.44% in both versions' Table 1; this is not evidence of a comparable performance decline.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds mathematical definitions of sub-question sets, answer/report mappings, and iterative report updates in equations (10)–(14). The original script-search objective and DS-STAR formulation are retained, mostly with expanded equation formatting. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contributions on heterogeneous-data analysis, sequential planning, and sufficiency verification. v4 reframes the abstract, introduction, and conclusion around both heterogeneous formats and open-ended research reports, adding DS-STAR+ and claims of leading performance on DABStep-Research. The original three-benchmark performance claims are retained.

C2.justification: v4 adds explanations linking report quality to factual sub-question answers and stronger foundation models, and argues that code-backed citations mitigate hallucination and enable human verification. It also interprets the new verifier tests as evidence of robustness and prompt generalizability. Existing retrieval and cost tradeoffs and the human-in-the-loop future direction remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 supplies DS-STAR+ pseudocode and four concrete prompts for initial/refinement question generation and report writing (Appendices C and M), specifies module-level model choices and refinement budget, and provides a BigQuery implementation example. Latency reporting is added. Original core prompts and execution logs are retained, although the earlier mmc4.xlsx analyzer-code example is removed.

R1.justification: v4 adds the DeepAnalyze citation and a focused discussion contrasting its fine-tuning approach with DS-STAR's use of foundation models without fine-tuning. It also qualifies the Text-to-SQL contrast by acknowledging DS-STAR's SQL capability. The remaining related-work coverage and principal comparisons are largely retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten around well-defined versus open-ended queries. The original method subsections are consolidated, refinement analysis is incorporated into the ablation section, and experiments are organized into separate query categories. The qualitative comparison moves to an appendix, and appendix organization changes extensively.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the original introductory illustration/radar summary and detailed workflow graphic with a new two-part DS-STAR/DS-STAR+ overview. It adds report-score, preference, refinement, and spreadsheet figures, expands sensitivity and cost tables, and separates model compatibility from component ablations. The original ReAct case moves to Appendix B, while the refinement plots and DA-Code example chart are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens validation through previously missing verifier tests, broader robustness checks, and latency reporting, while documenting DS-STAR+ with reproducible algorithms and prompts. These are useful gains beyond simply adding tasks. However, report comparisons use different underlying models, and strong grounding claims exceed the evidence: Appendix G's second report states 7.79% overall fraud while describing approximately 5.2% as the highest device-specific rate. The added validation and documentation support a net improvement, but these weaknesses limit its magnitude.
